rules.title: Details of processing
rules.requirement: The contract sets out the subject-matter and duration of the processing, the nature and purpose of the processing, the type of personal data and categories of data subjects, and the obligations and rights of the controller.
elements: obligations and rights of the controller
rules.whyItMatters: Art. 28(3) requires the contract to describe what is processed, about whom, why and for how long. Without it, the scope of the processor's mandate is unclear.
rules.suggestedAsk: Please provide the description of processing: subject-matter, duration, nature and purpose, types of personal data and categories of data subjects.

rules.title: Documented instructions
rules.requirement: The processor processes the personal data only on documented instructions from the controller, including with regard to transfers of personal data to a third country or an international organisation, unless required to do so by Union or Member State law; in such a case it informs the controller of that legal requirement before processing, unless that law prohibits such information.
elements: instructions cover transfers to third countries
informs the controller of a legal requirement to process otherwise
rules.whyItMatters: The processor may act only on the controller's documented instructions, including for international transfers. Without this clause the processor could use the data for its own purposes.
rules.suggestedAsk: Please confirm that you process personal data only on our documented instructions, including for transfers outside the EEA, and that you will inform us before processing if the law requires otherwise.

rules.title: Infringing instructions
rules.requirement: The processor immediately informs the controller if, in its opinion, an instruction infringes the GDPR or other Union or Member State data protection provisions.
rules.whyItMatters: The processor must warn the controller about instructions it believes are unlawful, so the controller can correct them.
rules.suggestedAsk: Please confirm that you will immediately inform us if, in your opinion, an instruction infringes data protection law.

rules.title: Confidentiality of personnel
rules.requirement: The processor ensures that persons authorised to process the personal data have committed themselves to confidentiality or are under an appropriate statutory obligation of confidentiality.
elements: committed to confidentiality or under statutory obligation
rules.whyItMatters: Everyone at the processor who handles the data must be bound to confidentiality. Without it, staff access is not contractually controlled.
rules.suggestedAsk: Please confirm that all persons authorised to process our personal data are bound by a confidentiality commitment or a statutory duty of confidentiality.

rules.title: Security of processing
rules.requirement: The processor takes all measures required pursuant to Article 32 (security of processing).
rules.whyItMatters: The processor must implement the security measures required by Art. 32. The contract should commit to them, usually with a description in an annex.
rules.suggestedAsk: Please confirm your commitment to the security measures required by Art. 32 GDPR and provide the description of your technical and organisational measures.

rules.title: Authorisation of sub-processors
rules.requirement: The processor does not engage another processor without prior specific or general written authorisation of the controller. Under general written authorisation, the processor informs the controller of any intended changes concerning the addition or replacement of other processors, giving the controller the opportunity to object.
elements: prior specific or general written authorisation
rules.whyItMatters: The controller must keep control over who else processes the data. Under a general authorisation, the controller must be told about changes and be able to object.
rules.suggestedAsk: Please confirm how sub-processors are authorised, how you notify us of intended changes, and how we can object.

rules.title: Conditions for engaging sub-processors
rules.requirement: The processor respects the conditions referred to in paragraphs 2 and 4 of Article 28 for engaging another processor.
rules.whyItMatters: The contract must bind the processor to the rules on authorisation and flow-down when it engages sub-processors.
rules.suggestedAsk: Please confirm that you will engage sub-processors only under the conditions of Art. 28(2) and 28(4) GDPR.

rules.title: Flow-down and liability for sub-processors
rules.requirement: The same data protection obligations as in the contract with the controller are imposed on the sub-processor by contract; the initial processor remains fully liable to the controller for the performance of the sub-processor's obligations.
elements: same data protection obligations imposed by contract
rules.whyItMatters: Sub-processors must be bound by the same obligations, and the processor stays liable for them. Otherwise protection weakens down the chain.
rules.suggestedAsk: Please confirm that sub-processors are bound by the same data protection obligations by contract and that you remain fully liable for their performance.

rules.title: Assistance with data subject rights
rules.requirement: Taking into account the nature of the processing, the processor assists the controller by appropriate technical and organisational measures, insofar as possible, to respond to requests for exercising the data subject's rights laid down in Chapter III.
elements: requests from data subjects exercising their rights
rules.whyItMatters: The controller must answer access, deletion and other rights requests within legal deadlines. It needs the processor's help to do so.
rules.suggestedAsk: Please confirm how you will assist us in responding to data subject rights requests, including timelines.

rules.title: Assistance with Articles 32 to 36
rules.requirement: The processor assists the controller in ensuring compliance with the obligations pursuant to Articles 32 to 36 (security, breach notification and communication, data protection impact assessment, prior consultation), taking into account the nature of processing and the information available to the processor.
rules.whyItMatters: The controller relies on the processor to meet security, breach notification and DPIA obligations. The contract must commit the processor to help.
rules.suggestedAsk: Please confirm your assistance with security, personal data breach notification, DPIAs and prior consultation (Art. 32 to 36 GDPR).

rules.title: Deletion or return at end of services
rules.requirement: At the choice of the controller, the processor deletes or returns all the personal data to the controller after the end of the provision of services relating to processing, and deletes existing copies unless Union or Member State law requires storage of the personal data.
elements: delete or return all personal data
delete existing copies unless law requires storage
hints: end of the provision of services
rules.whyItMatters: When the service ends, the controller decides whether data is deleted or returned. Without this clause, data may stay with the processor indefinitely.
rules.suggestedAsk: Please confirm that at the end of services you will, at our choice, delete or return all personal data and delete existing copies unless the law requires storage.

rules.title: Information and audits
rules.requirement: The processor makes available to the controller all information necessary to demonstrate compliance with the obligations of Article 28 and allows for and contributes to audits, including inspections, conducted by the controller or another auditor mandated by the controller.
elements: makes available information necessary to demonstrate compliance
allows for and contributes to audits, including inspections
rules.whyItMatters: The controller must be able to verify the processor's compliance, through information and audits including inspections.
rules.suggestedAsk: Please confirm the controller's audit and inspection rights and the process for exercising them.

rules.title: Breach notice time limit
rules.requirement: The contract states a specific time limit (for example a number of hours) for the processor to notify the controller of a personal data breach. Art. 33(2) itself says 'without undue delay'.
rules.whyItMatters: The controller has 72 hours to notify the supervisory authority. A specific processor deadline makes that achievable.
rules.suggestedAsk: Please state the maximum time in hours within which you will notify us of a personal data breach.

rules.title: Transfer mechanism
rules.requirement: Where personal data leaves the EEA, the contract names the transfer mechanism (Standard Contractual Clauses, an adequacy decision or the EU-US Data Privacy Framework).
rules.whyItMatters: Transfers outside the EEA need a legal mechanism under Chapter V. The contract should say which one applies.
rules.suggestedAsk: Please confirm whether personal data leaves the EEA and which transfer mechanism applies.

rules.title: Sub-processor list
rules.requirement: A list of sub-processors with name, purpose and location.
rules.whyItMatters: A list with purpose and location lets the controller assess each sub-processor and any transfers.
rules.suggestedAsk: Please provide your current sub-processor list with each entity's purpose and processing location.

rules.title: Retention period after termination
rules.requirement: A specific period within which personal data is deleted or returned after termination, including backups.
rules.whyItMatters: A concrete period makes the deletion obligation checkable.
rules.suggestedAsk: Please state within how many days after termination personal data, including backups, is deleted or returned.

rules.title: Data protection liability
rules.requirement: Liability or indemnity terms relating to data protection.
rules.whyItMatters: Liability terms decide who bears the cost of a data protection failure.
rules.suggestedAsk: Please confirm how liability for data protection breaches is allocated.

rules.title: AI training on customer data
rules.requirement: A statement on whether customer personal data is used to train or improve AI or machine learning models.
rules.whyItMatters: Use of customer data to train models is a separate purpose that the controller must know about and authorise.
rules.suggestedAsk: Please confirm whether our personal data is used to train or improve any AI or machine learning model, yours or a provider's.

rules.title: Privacy contact
rules.requirement: A data protection officer or privacy contact is named.
rules.whyItMatters: A named contact speeds up rights requests, incidents and audits.
rules.suggestedAsk: Please name your data protection officer or privacy contact.

rules.title: EU representative
rules.requirement: Where the processor is not established in the EU, an EU representative is named.
rules.whyItMatters: Non-EU processors subject to the GDPR generally must designate a representative in the EU.
rules.suggestedAsk: If you are not established in the EU, please name your EU representative.
